basis: Inherited thyroid hormone synthesis defect causing congenital hypothyroidism; neurologic damage is not established as common.
Congenital isolated loss of smell; olfaction belongs to the neurologic axis.
Ependymal tumour arising in the central nervous system.
Primary breast carcinoma; breast has no axis.
Umbrella for inherited immune deficiencies with abnormal immunoglobulin production; organ damage varies among subtypes.
Mitochondrial ATP synthesis disorder; neurologic damage is common (>30%) across Leigh and neuropathy/ataxia presentations; retinal involvement varies.
Peripheral nerve demyelination causes pressure palsies; weakness is neurogenic, scoliosis secondary; hearing loss occurs in 5-29%.
Acquired selective erythroid marrow failure, usually immune-mediated; anemia symptoms do not establish damage to other organs.
Malignant neoplasm of the lung hilum.
Central movement disorder causing dystonia; muscle contractions and abnormal postures do not establish primary muscle damage.
Meningeal tumour at the upper clivus; skull-base location does not establish bone involvement.
Transmissible prion disorders cause progressive spongiform degeneration of the central nervous system.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability characterize 6p deletion syndromes; eye, hearing and cardiac defects vary with deletion extent and subtype.
Sarcoma originating in the heart; soft-tissue histology does not establish skeletal muscle involvement.
Adenocarcinoma arising in the gallbladder, included in the hepatic axis.
Gonococcal infection of the cervix; the reproductive site has no organ axis, but the infectious mechanism applies.
Neuroblastoma originates from sympathetic neural tissue; increased dopamine excretion alone does not establish endocrine organ damage.
Disorders of protein synthesis, folding and clearance; affected organs vary across this broad metabolic umbrella.
Congenital absence of kidneys and ureters; pulmonary hypoplasia, cardiac and skeletal anomalies occur in 5-29%.
Multiple schwannomas arise from peripheral or spinal nerve sheaths; skin ancestry does not establish intrinsic skin disease.
Inherited retinal degeneration causing night blindness, field constriction and progressive visual loss.
Autoimmune cutaneous disease with permanent scarring, dyspigmentation and alopecia; systemic lupus is a separate disease.
Disease of the lacrimal gland, part of the ocular apparatus; immune mechanisms apply only to some subtypes.
Cerebellar malformation and developmental disability; esotropia affects 5/13 (~38%), supporting ocular dysfunction; renal insufficiency affects 2/13 (~15%), below threshold.
Primary distal skeletal myopathy with progressive weakness, muscle atrophy and myopathic abnormalities.
